title: hp finite elements and spectral elements

items.title: Endpoint-preserving integrated Legendre projector
items.statement:
For $p\ge1$ and $g\in L^2(-1,1)$, define the degree-$(p-1)$ Legendre orthogonal projection
$$
\Pi_{p-1}g:=\sum_{n=0}^{p-1}\frac{2n+1}{2}\left(\int_{-1}^1g(t)P_n(t)\,dt\right)P_n.
$$
For $c\in\mathbb R$, define the endpoint-anchored integrated projector
$$
\mathcal I_p(c,g)(x):=c+\int_{-1}^x\Pi_{p-1}g(t)\,dt,\qquad -1\le x\le1.
$$
If an absolutely continuous function $f$ is represented as $f(x)=f(-1)+\int_{-1}^xf'(t)\,dt$ with $f'\in L^2$, write $I_pf:=\mathcal I_p(f(-1),f')$. The finite sum and integral are defined for every such input; no choice axiom is used in this definition.

references.title: Joachim Schöberl, Numerical Methods for Partial Differential Equations, p-version FEM
references.locator: §§30.1–30.4: Legendre projection and endpoint-preserving integrated polynomial interpolation.

references.title: Leszek F. Demkowicz, Mathematical Theory of Finite Elements

items.title: Variable-degree conforming hp spaces on matching affine meshes
items.statement:
Let $d\ge2$ and let $\mathcal T$ be a finite matching affine simplicial mesh of a bounded polyhedral open set $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d$ in the sense of [[def-matching-affine-simplicial-meshes]]. A **degree map** is a function $p:\mathcal T\to\mathbb N_0$ with finite values. The broken simplex space associated with $(\mathcal T,p)$ is
$$
V^{\mathrm{br}}(\mathcal T,p):=\{v\in L^2(\Omega):v|_K\in\mathbb P_{p_K}(K)\text{ for every }K\in\mathcal T\},
$$
where $p_K:=p(K)$ and $\mathbb P_m(K)$ denotes restrictions of real polynomials of total degree at most $m$. Its **conforming hp space** is the subspace of functions whose two polynomial traces agree on every interior facet. The zero-boundary hp space further requires the polynomial trace to vanish on every boundary facet. For an interior facet $F=K\cap K'$, its trace degree is $p_F:=\min(p_K,p_{K'})$; equality of the two traces means that their common polynomial belongs to $\mathbb P_{p_F}(F)$.

A **matching affine tensor-box mesh** is a finite face-to-face partition of a bounded polytope into affine images of $[-1,1]^d$, with pairwise disjoint interiors. For a scalar degree $p_K$ on each box, the local tensor space is $\mathbb Q_{p_K}(K)$, the pullback of polynomials of degree at most $p_K$ in each reference coordinate. The conforming box hp space is defined by equality of polynomial traces across every shared face, and its zero-boundary subspace by zero traces on the exterior faces. For a shared face $F=K\cap K'$, set $p_F=\min(p_K,p_{K'})$; its common trace lies in $\mathbb Q_{p_F}(F)$ in tangential reference coordinates. This definition of tensor boxes does not include curved or non-affine cells.

On either mesh, **h-refinement** replaces one cell by a finite matching partition of that cell and assigns degrees to the children; **p-refinement** raises at least one cell degree while leaving the mesh fixed; **hp-refinement** performs both operations. A local polynomial basis is **hierarchical** if its ordered degree layers span the nested spaces $\mathbb P_0\subset\cdots\subset\mathbb P_p$ (or $\mathbb Q_0\subset\cdots\subset\mathbb Q_p$), with each new layer extending the preceding span. For example, pullbacks of reference monomials $\widehat x^\nu$ ordered by $|\nu|$ give such a basis for $\mathbb P_p$, and tensor monomials $\xi^\nu$ ordered by $\max_i\nu_i$ give one for $\mathbb Q_p$. This basis convention does not assert stability of a particular basis or projector.

items.title: Legendre-Gauss-Lobatto nodes are distinct and interior critical points are simple
items.statement: For every integer $p\ge1$, the Legendre polynomial $P_p$ has exactly $p$ simple roots in $(-1,1)$, and $P_p'$ has exactly $p-1$ simple roots in $(-1,1)$, one between each consecutive pair of roots of $P_p$. Consequently, the $p+1$ nodes consisting of $-1$, $1$, and the roots of $P_p'$ are pairwise distinct.

references.title: Joachim Schöberl, Numerical Methods for Partial Differential Equations, p-version FEM
references.locator: §§30.1–30.2: Legendre polynomial family and p-version spectral points.

items.title: Weighted Jacobi endpoint kernel on the reference interval
items.statement:
For an integer $d\ge1$, put $w_d(t)=(1-t)^{d-1}$ on $[0,1]$ and, for $n\ge0$, define
$$\phi_n(t):=\frac{(-1)^n}{n!}(1-t)^{-(d-1)}\frac{d^n}{dt^n}\bigl(t^n(1-t)^{n+d-1}\bigr).$$
The quotient extends to a polynomial of degree $n$. These polynomials are pairwise orthogonal in $L^2(w_d\,dt)$, with
$$\phi_n(0)=(-1)^n,\qquad \operatorname{lc}(\phi_n)=\binom{2n+d-1}{n},\qquad \int_0^1w_d\phi_n^2\,dt=\frac1{2n+d}.$$
Consequently, for every $p\ge0$ the squared norm of endpoint evaluation $q\mapsto q(0)$ on $\mathbb P_p([0,1])$ with this weighted $L^2$ norm is exactly $(p+1)(p+d)$.

references.title: Leszek F. Demkowicz, Mathematical Theory of Finite Elements
references.locator: §3.1.4, printed pp. 64–68: Jacobi-based hierarchical p-version functions and endpoint degrees of freedom.

references.title: Tim Warburton and Jan S. Hesthaven, On the Constants in hp-Finite Element Trace Inverse Inequalities
references.locator: §§3–4, pp. 4–14: Jacobi endpoint evaluation and its use in explicit simplex trace bounds.

items.title: Weighted simplex polynomial projection has explicit p-rates
items.statement:
Let $\widehat K$ be the reference simplex of [[def-matching-affine-simplicial-meshes]], let $\alpha=(\alpha_0,\ldots,\alpha_d)$ have nonnegative real entries, and let $\omega_\alpha=\prod_{j=0}^d\lambda_j^{\alpha_j}$, where $\lambda_j$ are its barycentric coordinates. Give polynomials the inner product $\langle f,g\rangle_\alpha=\int_{\widehat K}\omega_\alpha fg$. Put $\mathbb P_{-1}=\{0\}$ and let $E_n=\mathbb P_n(\widehat K)\ominus\mathbb P_{n-1}(\widehat K)$ in this weighted inner product. For a finite sum $u=\sum_{n\ge0}u_n$, $u_n\in E_n$, define
$$
\|u\|_{\mathcal H_\alpha^s}^2:=\sum_{n\ge0}(1+\mu_n)^s\|u_n\|_{L^2(\omega_\alpha)}^2,\qquad \mu_n=n(n+d+|\alpha|),
$$
and define $\mathcal H_\alpha^s$ as the completion of these finite sums. If $m\ge\ell\ge0$, its orthogonal degree truncation $P_pu=\sum_{n=0}^pu_n$ obeys
$$
\|u-P_pu\|_{\mathcal H_\alpha^\ell}\le(1+\mu_{p+1})^{-(m-\ell)/2}\|u\|_{\mathcal H_\alpha^m}.
$$
For $q\in\mathbb P_p(\widehat K)$, $\|q\|_{\mathcal H_\alpha^m}\le(1+\mu_p)^{(m-\ell)/2}\|q\|_{\mathcal H_\alpha^\ell}$. These are estimates in the explicitly coefficient-defined scale $\mathcal H_\alpha^s$; they do not identify that scale with ordinary unweighted $H^s(\widehat K)$.

references.title: Matthias Braess and Christoph Schwab, Approximation on polyhedral domains with geometric meshes
references.locator: §3, Theorem 3.3 and proof, printed pp. 6–8: weighted simplex orthogonal degree layers and eigenvalues n(n+d+|alpha|).

references.title: Leszek F. Demkowicz, Mathematical Theory of Finite Elements

items.title: A degree-uniform polynomial edge lift with the strong edge norm
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $p\in\mathbb N_0$, let $T=\{(x,y):x>0,\ y>0,\ x+y<1\}$, and let $q$ be a real polynomial of degree at most $p$ satisfying $q(0)=q(1)=0$. Define the polynomial $R(t)=q(t)/t$ by cancellation at $t=0$, and put

$$
Lq(x,y)=q(x)-xR(1-y).
$$

Then $Lq\in\mathbb P_p(T)$, it equals $q$ on $y=0$, and it vanishes on $x=0$ and $x+y=1$. Moreover,

$$
\|Lq\|_{H^1(T)}\le4\|q'\|_{L^2(0,1)},
$$

independently of $p$. Permuting the three vertices gives the same bound, up to one fixed constant, for each reference edge. If $K$ is a shape-regular affine triangle, $E$ is an edge of length $\ell_E$, and $h_K=\operatorname{diam}(K)$, the transported lift satisfies

$$
|L_Eq|_{H^1(K)}\le C_\gamma\ell_E^{1/2}\|\partial_\tau q\|_{L^2(E)},\qquad \|L_Eq\|_{L^2(K)}\le C_\gamma h_K\ell_E^{1/2}\|\partial_\tau q\|_{L^2(E)}.
$$

Consequently continuous polynomial data on the three edges of a triangle, each of degree at most the cell degree, have a polynomial extension of that cell degree. The estimate uses the strong $H^1$ edge norm and asserts no optimal $H^{1/2}$ trace-lifting bound.

references.title: Joachim Schöberl, Numerical Methods for Partial Differential Equations, Chapter 30: hp Finite Elements
references.locator: §30.4.2, projection-based interpolation on triangles. The source states a p-stable H^(1/2) extension but leaves major steps as exercises; this item proves an explicit, different H^1-edge-norm lift.

references.title: Martin Vohralík, Finite Element Methods, Chapter 6: hp finite elements
references.locator: §§6.1–6.3, printed pp. 54–57: conforming hp spaces and the stated (but incompletely derived) simplex approximation context. The formula below is proved locally.

items.title: An ordinary derivative controls the Legendre tail with a factorial ratio
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice for the $k\ge1$ branch. Let $P_n$ be the real Legendre polynomial normalized by $P_n(1)=1$, and let $\Pi_N$ be the $L^2(-1,1;\mathbb R)$ orthogonal projection onto $\mathbb P_N(-1,1)$. For every integer $k\ge1$, every integer $N\ge k-1$, and every real-valued $f\in H^k(-1,1)$,

$$
\|f-\Pi_Nf\|_{L^2(-1,1)}\le\left(\frac{(N+1-k)!}{(N+1+k)!}\right)^{1/2}\|f^{(k)}\|_{L^2(-1,1)}.
$$

For $k=0$, every integer $N\ge0$, and $f\in L^2(-1,1)$, $\|f-\Pi_Nf\|_2\le\|f\|_2$. For $n,m\ge k$ the repeated derivative orthogonality identity is

$$
\int_{-1}^1(1-x^2)^kP_n^{(k)}(x)P_m^{(k)}(x)\,dx=\frac{2}{2n+1}\frac{(n+k)!}{(n-k)!}\,\delta_{nm}.
$$

references.title: Shen and Tang, Spectral and High-Order Methods with Applications
references.locator: Chapter 1, §1.8, printed pp. 61–67: Jacobi/Legendre projection estimates, derivative orthogonality, and the weighted Sobolev scale. The exact ordinary unweighted factorial estimate is proved locally here.

references.title: Joachim Schöberl, Numerical Methods for Partial Differential Equations, Chapter 30: hp Finite Elements
references.locator: §30.4.2, projection-based interpolation on triangles and the Legendre tail estimate; the higher-order derivative identity is completed locally here.

items.title: Analytic derivative bounds give exponential polynomial approximation on a triangle
items.statement:
Let $S$ be the closed reference triangle $\overline T$, where $T=\{x,y>0,x+y<1\}$, or the closed interval $[0,1]$, and let $f:S\to\mathbb R$ be real-valued. Write $\mathbb P_p(S)$ for restrictions of real polynomials of total degree at most $p$ on the triangle and degree at most $p$ on the interval. Say that $f$ is smooth up to $S$ when every partial derivative on the interior has a continuous extension to $S$. Suppose that for some $M>0$ and $A\ge1$,

$$
\|D^\alpha f\|_{L^\infty(S)}\le M A^{|\alpha|}|\alpha|!\qquad\text{for every multi-index }\alpha.
$$

Use $\|g\|_{W^{1,\infty}(S)}:=\|g\|_{L^\infty(S)}+\sum_{i=1}^{\dim S}\|\partial_i g\|_{L^\infty(S)}$. Then constants $C,b>0$, depending only on $A$ and the fixed reference domain, satisfy

$$
\inf_{q\in\mathbb P_p(S)}\|f-q\|_{W^{1,\infty}(S)}\le CM e^{-bp}\qquad(p\ge1).
$$

For the interval branch there is also an endpoint-preserving polynomial $J_pf\in\mathbb P_p([0,1])$ whose derivative is the $L^2$ orthogonal projection of $f'$ onto $\mathbb P_{p-1}$. It satisfies $\|(J_pf)'\|_2\le\|f'\|_2$ and $\|f-J_pf\|_{H^1}\le CM e^{-bp}$ after changing $C,b$ by constants depending only on $A$.

references.title: Yanchen He, Paul Houston, Christoph Schwab, and Thomas P. Wihler, Exponential Convergence of hp-ILGFEM, version 1
references.locator: §§2.3 and 4.1, PDF pp. 5–11: analytic corner classes and exponential hp approximation context. The polynomial-mask construction below is independent and supplies its local approximation step.

references.title: Shen and Tang, Spectral and High-Order Methods with Applications

items.title: Weighted analytic polygon functions have corner decay and scaled analytic bounds
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^2$ be a bounded open polygonal domain with finitely many straight sides and corner set $\mathcal C=\{c_1,\ldots,c_m\}$, with interior angle at each corner strictly between $0$ and $2\pi$. Let $0\le\beta_i<1$ and write $\Phi_\gamma(x)=\prod_{i=1}^m|x-c_i|^{\gamma_i}$ for a vector $\gamma\in[0,\infty)^m$. For integer $k\ge2$, define

$$
\|v\|_{H^{k,2}_\beta(\Omega)}^2=\|v\|_{H^1(\Omega)}^2+\sum_{j=2}^k\sum_{|\alpha|=j}\|\Phi_{\beta+j-2}D^\alpha v\|_{L^2(\Omega)}^2,
$$

where $(\beta+j-2)_i=\beta_i+j-2$ and a zero exponent contributes the factor one. Let $u\in H^{k,2}_\beta(\Omega)$ for every integer $k\ge2$, with real-valued weak derivatives, and suppose constants $C_u,d_u>0$ satisfy

$$
\left\|\Phi_{\beta+j-2}\sum_{|\alpha|=j}|D^\alpha u|\right\|_{L^2(\Omega)}\le C_ud_u^{j-2}(j-2)!\qquad(j\ge2).
$$

For each fixed $0<a<\min_i(1-\beta_i)$ there are constants $C,A,R>0$ such that the weak class of $u$ has a unique representative $\widetilde u\in C(\overline\Omega)$, smooth up to every open side away from corners, and for $0<r=|x-c_i|<R$,

$$
|\widetilde u(x)-\widetilde u(c_i)|\le Cr^a,\qquad |D^\alpha\widetilde u(x)|\le CA^{|\alpha|}|\alpha|!r^{a-|\alpha|}\quad(|\alpha|\ge1).
$$

On every compact subset of $\overline\Omega\setminus\mathcal C$, the derivatives satisfy ordinary factorial bounds $|D^\alpha u|\le C_0A_0^{|\alpha|}|\alpha|!$. On every closed nondegenerate shape-regular affine triangle $K\subset\overline\Omega$ with $K^\circ\subset\Omega$ and $K\cap\mathcal C=\varnothing$, whose ratio $h_K/\operatorname{dist}(K,\mathcal C)$ is bounded above and below by fixed positive constants, where $\operatorname{dist}(K,\mathcal C)=\inf_{x\in K,c\in\mathcal C}|x-c|$, set $r_K=\min(R,\operatorname{dist}(K,\mathcal C))$. After subtracting a suitable constant from the pullback $\widehat u$ to the reference triangle of [[def-matching-affine-simplicial-meshes]], $\|D^\alpha\widehat u\|_\infty\le C A_1^{|\alpha|}|\alpha|!r_K^a$ for every multi-index $\alpha$, with constants uniform over this family. If a closed nondegenerate shape-regular affine triangle $K\subset\overline\Omega$ with $K^\circ\subset\Omega$, diameter $h<R$, has a corner $c_i$ as a vertex, its vertex affine interpolant $a_K$ satisfies

$$
|u-a_K|_{H^1(K)}\le Ch^a,\qquad \|u-a_K\|_{L^2(K)}\le Ch^{a+1}.
$$

references.locator: §2.3, equation (12), Definition 1, and the continuity assertion preceding it, PDF pp. 5–6: weighted corner regularity and its continuity context. The quantitative pointwise bounds are proved locally here.

items.title: Legendre-Gauss-Lobatto nodes, weights, and tensor quadrature
items.statement:
Fix an integer $p\ge1$. Let $\xi_0=-1$, $\xi_p=1$, and let $\xi_1<\cdots<\xi_{p-1}$ be the roots of $P_p'$ in $(-1,1)$; for $p=1$ this interior list is empty. By [[lem-legendre-gauss-lobatto-nodes-are-distinct]] these $p+1$ nodes are distinct. Define $\ell_j(x)=\prod_{0\le i\le p,\ i
e j}(x-\xi_i)/(\xi_j-\xi_i)$, set $w_j=\int_{-1}^1\ell_j(x)\,dx$, and define the **Legendre–Gauss–Lobatto rule** by $Q_p(f)=\sum_{j=0}^p w_jf(\xi_j)$.

On $[-1,1]^d$ its tensor rule is $Q_p^{\otimes d}(f)=\sum_{j_1,\ldots,j_d=0}^p(w_{j_1}\cdots w_{j_d})f(\xi_{j_1},\ldots,\xi_{j_d})$. For an affine box map $F_K(\xi)=b_K+J_K\xi$, define the transported rule by $Q_{K,p}(f)=|\det J_K|Q_p^{\otimes d}(f\circ F_K)$. The nodal basis on $K$ is the pullback of $\prod_{r=1}^d\ell_{j_r}(\xi_r)$. The local mass and stiffness forms are respectively $m_{K,p}(v,w)=Q_{K,p}(vw)$ and $a_{K,p}(v,w)=Q_{K,p}(
abla v\cdot
abla w)$; any sampled coefficient is evaluated at the same quadrature nodes. Global forms are assembled by summing the cell forms.

references.title: Joachim Schöberl, Numerical Methods for Partial Differential Equations, p-version FEM
references.locator: §§30.1–30.4: Legendre nodal bases, endpoint-preserving interpolation, and spectral p-version context.

references.title: Lloyd N. Trefethen, Short note on the mass matrix for Gauss-Lobatto grid points

items.title: Uniform-degree polygon corner spaces have cubic degree-of-freedom growth
items.statement:
For $k\ge1$, let a matching triangulation $\mathcal T_k$ of a polygon have at most $C_0k$ triangles. Assign a uniform total polynomial degree $p_k\ge1$ with $p_k\le C_1k$. The algebraic space of continuous piecewise $\mathbb P_{p_k}$ functions has dimension
$$
N_k\le C_2k^3,
$$
where $C_2$ depends only on $C_0$ and $C_1$. The same upper bound holds for any subspace imposing homogeneous boundary traces. This is an upper count only; it asserts no hp approximation rate.

references.title: Yanchen He, Paul Houston, Christoph Schwab, and Thomas P. Wihler, Exponential Convergence of hp-ILGFEM, version 1
references.locator: §4.1, equations (29)–(31), PDF pp. 10–11: at most O(k) triangles, uniform degree p_k proportional to k, and dimension O(k^3).

references.title: Leszek F. Demkowicz, Mathematical Theory of Finite Elements
references.locator: §3.1.4, printed pp. 64–68: local polynomial degree and dimension-layer conventions; the global count is proved here.

items.title: Matching variable-degree polynomial traces give an H1 function
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice. On a finite matching affine simplicial mesh or a finite face-to-face affine tensor-box mesh, a piecewise polynomial scalar function whose two traces agree on every interior facet belongs to $H^1(\Omega)$, and its weak gradient equals its ordinary cellwise polynomial gradient almost everywhere. The simplex degrees may vary by cell; the box degrees may also vary.

references.title: Jean-Luc Guermond, MATH 661 Fall 2019, Chapter 32, H1-conforming approximation
references.locator: §32.1, printed pp. 144–145: matching piecewise-polynomial traces and the H1-conforming space.

references.title: Luca Heltai, Numerical Methods for Partial Differential Equations, Lecture 2
references.locator: §10: continuity across matching faces and conforming finite-element functions.

items.title: Integrated Legendre projection gives an explicit p-rate in H1
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $p\ge1$, $s\ge0$, $g\in H_L^s$ as defined in [[def-legendre-weighted-sobolev-scale]], identified with its canonical $L^2(-1,1)$ class, and let $c\in\mathbb R$. Define $u(x)=c+\int_{-1}^xg(t)\,dt$ and $I_pu=\mathcal I_p(c,g)$ by [[def-hp-integrated-legendre-projector]]. Then $u$ and $I_pu$ are absolutely continuous, $I_pu\in\mathbb P_p$, and $I_pu(\pm1)=u(\pm1)$. Moreover,
$$\|u-I_pu\|_{H^1(-1,1)} \le\sqrt5\,(1+p(p+1))^{-s/2}\|g\|_{H_L^s},$$
where the displayed $H^1$ error norm is $\bigl(\|u-I_pu\|_{L^2}^2+\|g-\Pi_{p-1}g\|_{L^2}^2\bigr)^{1/2}$. This coefficient-scale assertion does not identify $H_L^s$ with an ordinary derivative-based Sobolev norm.

references.title: Joachim Schöberl, Numerical Methods for Partial Differential Equations, p-version FEM
references.locator: §§30.1–30.4: Legendre orthogonality and the integrated polynomial projection; the general simplex extension is not used as a proof here.

references.title: Leszek F. Demkowicz, Mathematical Theory of Finite Elements
references.locator: §3.1.4, printed pp. 64–68: hierarchical p-version bases and endpoint/edge degrees of freedom.

items.title: Degree-explicit polynomial trace inverse inequality on simplices
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), as required by the affine-scaling supplier used below.

Let $K$ be a nondegenerate $d$-simplex, $d\ge2$, let $F$ be one of its facets, and let $p\ge0$. For every $v\in\mathbb P_p(K)$,
$$
\|v\|_{L^2(F)}^2\le\frac{(p+1)(p+d)|F|}{d|K|}\|v\|_{L^2(K)}^2.
$$
If $K$ belongs to a shape-regular affine simplex family with $h_K=\operatorname{diam}(K)$ and shape bound $\sigma$, then
$$
\|v\|_{L^2(F)}^2\le C_{d,\sigma}\frac{(p+1)(p+d)}{h_K}\|v\|_{L^2(K)}^2.
$$
For $p\ge1$, the normal derivative of $v$ has degree at most $p-1$ on $K$ and satisfies the same inequalities with $(p+1)(p+d)$ replaced by $p(p+d-1)$. In particular, polynomial normal-flux trace penalties have the explicit scale $p(p+d-1)/h_K$; this is an inverse trace bound, not a p-approximation or a DG coercivity theorem.

references.title: Tim Warburton and Jan S. Hesthaven, On the Constants in hp-Finite Element Trace Inverse Inequalities
references.locator: §§3–4, pp. 4–14: exact Jacobi endpoint-kernel trace bounds on intervals, triangles, and simplices.

references.title: Jean-Luc Guermond, MATH 661 Fall 2025, Chapter 11, Local interpolation on affine meshes
references.locator: §11.1, printed pp. 117–119: affine simplex scaling and shape-regular face/volume factors.

items.title: Constructive ordinary Sobolev polynomial approximation on triangles
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $T=\{(x,y):x>0,\ y>0,\ x+y<1\}$, let $r\ge5$ be an integer, let $p\ge2r-4$ be an integer, and put $n=\lfloor p/2\rfloor$ and

$$
\eta_{n,r}=\left(\frac{(n-r+3)!}{(n+r-5)!}\right)^{1/2}.
$$

There is a bounded linear map $A_{p,r}:H^r(T;\mathbb R)\to\mathbb P_p(T;\mathbb R)$, where $\mathbb P_p(T;\mathbb R)$ is the restriction of real polynomials in $(x,y)$ of total degree at most $p$. It is explicitly defined in the proof from the reference-simplex extension, a unique moment polynomial, and finite Legendre projections, and satisfies

$$
\|u-A_{p,r}u\|_{H^2(T)}\le C_r\eta_{n,r}|u|_{H^r(T)}.
$$

Here $C_r$ is independent of $p$ and is the product of a fixed reference extension bound, the reference moment-projection bound, and an absolute tensor-projection constant; no useful growth bound in $r$ is asserted. For a shape-regular affine triangle $K$ of diameter $h_K$, affine transport gives

$$
\left(\sum_{j=0}^2h_K^{2j-2}|u-A_{K,p,r}u|_{H^j(K)}^2\right)^{1/2}\le C_{r,\gamma}\eta_{n,r}h_K^{r-1}|u|_{H^r(K)}.
$$

If $p\ge4(r-2)$, then $\eta_{n,r}\le(4/p)^{r-4}$. This is a conservative ordinary Sobolev rate; it is neither an optimal $p^{-(r-1)}$ estimate nor an analytic growth estimate for $C_r$.

references.title: Shen and Tang, Spectral and High-Order Methods with Applications
references.locator: Chapter 1, §1.8, printed pp. 61–67: ordinary and weighted polynomial projection estimates. The local tensor proof supplies the stated triangle construction.

references.title: Joachim Schöberl, Numerical Methods for Partial Differential Equations, Chapter 30: hp Finite Elements
references.locator: §30.4.2, projection-based triangle interpolation and the p-dependent Legendre tail. Major extension steps are left as exercises; this proof supplies the local construction and mixed-derivative accounting.

items.title: Analytic data converge exponentially under fixed-mesh p refinement
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega$ be partitioned by a fixed finite matching affine tensor-box mesh, and let $u\in C^1(\overline\Omega)$ be smooth on each box. For each cell $K$, let $\widehat u_K$ be its pullback to $[-1,1]^d$. Assume that for fixed constants $M>0$ and $R>1$,
$$
\sup_{\widehat x\in[-1,1]^d}|\partial^\nu\widehat u_K(\widehat x)|\le M|\nu|!R^{-|\nu|}
$$
for every multi-index $\nu\in\mathbb N_0^d$ and every cell $K$. Choose any $q$ with $R^{-1}<q<1$. For each common degree $p\ge1$, tensorize the endpoint-preserving integrated Legendre projector of [[def-hp-integrated-legendre-projector]] on each reference cell and transport it to $K$, obtaining $u_p$. Then the cell traces of $u_p$ agree across every shared face and
$$
\|u-u_p\|_{H^1(\Omega)}\le C_{\mathcal T,d,R,q}M q^p.
$$
The constant may depend on the fixed mesh; the estimate is a p-rate on a fixed mesh and makes no claim about h-refinement.

items.title: Constructive varying-degree triangle interpolation in unweighted H1
items.statement:
Assume Full Choice. Let $\mathcal T$ be a finite matching shape-regular affine triangulation in two dimensions, let each cell $K$ have an arbitrary finite total degree $p_K\ge1$, and let $u\in C(\overline\Omega;\mathbb R)$ satisfy $u|_K\in H^2(K)$ for every cell. For every edge $E$, let $\tau_E$ be either unit tangent direction and write $\partial_{\tau_E}v=\nabla v\cdot\tau_E$. For an interior edge $E=K\cap K'$, set $p_E=\min(p_K,p_{K'})$; for a boundary edge of $K$, set $p_E=p_K$. Put $m_K=\min_{E\subset\partial K}p_E$. There is a linear interpolant $I_{\mathcal T,p}u$ in the trace-matching space of [[def-hp-variable-degree-spaces-on-matching-meshes]]. It preserves any zero boundary edge data: if $u$ vanishes on a boundary edge, so does $I_{\mathcal T,p}u$. For every $q\in\mathbb P_{m_K}(K;\mathbb R)$,

$$
|u-I_{\mathcal T,p}u|_{H^1(K)}\le |u-q|_{H^1(K)}+C_\gamma\sum_{E\subset\partial K}\left(\ell_E^{-1/2}\|u-q\|_{L^2(E)}+\ell_E^{1/2}\|\partial_{\tau_E}(u-q)\|_{L^2(E)}\right),
$$

and

$$
h_K^{-1}\|u-I_{\mathcal T,p}u\|_{L^2(K)}+|u-I_{\mathcal T,p}u|_{H^1(K)} \le C_\gamma\left(h_K^{-1}\|u-q\|_{L^2(K)}+|u-q|_{H^1(K)}+\sum_{E\subset\partial K}\left(\ell_E^{-1/2}\|u-q\|_{L^2(E)}+\ell_E^{1/2}\|\partial_{\tau_E}(u-q)\|_{L^2(E)}\right)\right).
$$

The constant is independent of the degrees and their ratios. In particular, if integer $r\ge5$, $m_K\ge2r-4$, $n_K=\lfloor m_K/2\rfloor$, and $u|_K\in H^r(K)$, then

$$
|u-I_{\mathcal T,p}u|_{H^1(K)}\le C_{r,\gamma}h_K^{r-1}\left(\frac{(n_K-r+3)!}{(n_K+r-5)!}\right)^{1/2}|u|_{H^r(K)}.
$$

For $m_K\ge4(r-2)$ the factorial factor is at most $(4/m_K)^{r-4}$. The effective degree $m_K$ records the lowest degree among the shared edge traces; no rate independent of neighboring trace degrees is asserted.

items.title: GLL quadrature changes only the top Legendre modes and is p-uniformly equivalent
items.statement:
For every $p\ge1$, the one-dimensional GLL rule integrates all polynomials of degree at most $2p-1$ exactly and has positive weights. If $f=\sum_{n=0}^pa_nP_n$, then
$$Q_p(f^2)-\int_{-1}^1f^2= rac{2(p+1)}{p(2p+1)}a_p^2.$$
For every $v\in\mathbb Q_p([-1,1]^d)$,
$$\|v\|_{L^2}^2\le Q_p^{\otimes d}(v^2)\le3^d\|v\|_{L^2}^2,\qquad \|
abla v\|_{L^2}^2\le Q_p^{\otimes d}(|
abla v|^2)\le3^d\|
abla v\|_{L^2}^2.$$
The same inequalities hold on affine boxes under the transported rule. If a pointwise-defined scalar coefficient $a:\overline K	o\mathbb R$ is Lebesgue measurable on $K$ and satisfies $0<\underline a\le a(x)\le\overline a$ throughout $\overline K$, the sampled form $Q_{K,p}(a|
abla v|^2)$ is equivalent to the exact weighted energy $\int_Ka|
abla v|^2$ with lower factor $\underline a/\overline a$ and upper factor $3^d\overline a/\underline a$. These are p-uniform stability bounds; they do not bound the Strang consistency defect or equate quadrature with exact Galerkin assembly.

items.title: Exponential hp energy convergence for weighted-analytic polygon corners
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^2$ be a bounded polygonal open domain with finite corner set $\mathcal C=\{c_1,\ldots,c_m\}$ and weights $0\le\beta_i<1$. For $\gamma\in[0,\infty)^m$ define $\Phi_\gamma(x)=\prod_i|x-c_i|^{\gamma_i}$; $\beta+j-2$ means componentwise addition. For integer $k\ge2$, define

$$
\|v\|_{H^{k,2}_\beta(\Omega)}^2=\|v\|_{H^1(\Omega)}^2+\sum_{j=2}^k\sum_{|\alpha|=j}\|\Phi_{\beta+j-2}D^\alpha v\|_2^2.
$$

Let $B^2_\beta(\Omega)$ consist of real-valued functions in every $H^{k,2}_\beta(\Omega)$ for which some $C_u,d_u>0$ satisfy

$$
\left\|\Phi_{\beta+k-2}\sum_{|\alpha|=k}|D^\alpha u|\right\|_2\le C_ud_u^{k-2}(k-2)!\qquad(k\ge2).
$$

Let $(\mathcal T_k)_{k\ge1}$ be nested finite matching shape-regular affine triangulations of $\Omega$, with at most $C_0k$ triangles. Write $h_T=\operatorname{diam}(T)$ and $\operatorname{dist}(T,\mathcal C)=\inf_{x\in T,c\in\mathcal C}|x-c|$. Assume a fixed $0<\sigma<1$ and $C_1>0$ satisfy

$$
\sigma\le\frac{h_T}{\operatorname{dist}(T,\mathcal C)}\le\sigma^{-1}\quad(\overline T\cap\mathcal C=\varnothing),\qquad h_T\le C_1\sigma^k\quad(\overline T\cap\mathcal C\ne\varnothing).
$$

Let $p_k\in\mathbb N$ be uniform total polynomial degrees with $c_0k\le p_k\le c_1k$ for fixed $0<c_0\le c_1$. For a fixed union $\Gamma_D$ of polygon edges, let $V_k$ be the space of broken piecewise-$\mathbb P_{p_k}$ functions whose polynomial traces agree on every interior edge and vanish on the boundary edges in $\Gamma_D$; put $N_k=\dim V_k$. This is the corresponding subspace of the variable-degree space in [[def-hp-variable-degree-spaces-on-matching-meshes]].
For this smoother class, the boundary condition means that the unique continuous representative supplied by [[lem-hp-weighted-analytic-corner-pointwise-control]] vanishes pointwise on the edges in $\Gamma_D$; no zero condition is imposed on the other edges. If $u\in B^2_\beta(\Omega)$ satisfies this boundary condition, then constants $C,b>0$, independent of $k$, satisfy

$$
\inf_{v_k\in V_k}\|\nabla(u-v_k)\|_{L^2(\Omega)}\le Ce^{-bN_k^{1/3}}.
$$

For a bounded coercive conforming Galerkin problem on a Hilbert space $V\subset H^1(\Omega)$, assume $u\in V$ is its exact variational solution: $a(u,v)=F(v)$ for every $v\in V$, with bounded load $F$. If $V_k\subset V$ and the norm on $V$ is equivalent to the gradient seminorm, Céa's estimate gives the same exponential rate for the energy error, with its actual $M/\alpha$ and norm-equivalence factors included. The constants may depend on the polygon, weights, weighted analytic bounds, mesh shape and grading constants, degree constants, $\Gamma_D$, and the Galerkin coercivity and norm-equivalence constants.

items.title: Cea transfers the fixed-mesh analytic p rate to the energy error
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. On a fixed finite matching affine tensor-box mesh, let $V=H^1(\Omega)$ with its standard norm, let $a(v,w)=\int_\Omega(\nabla v\cdot\nabla w+vw)$, and let $F$ be a bounded linear functional on $V$. Let $u\in V$ solve $a(u,w)=F(w)$ for all $w\in V$, and let $u_p$ be its conforming Galerkin solution in the common-degree trace-matching tensor space of [[def-hp-variable-degree-spaces-on-matching-meshes]]. If the analytic hypotheses of [[thm-hp-analytic-p-convergence-on-fixed-tensor-mesh]] hold with constants $M,R$ and $R^{-1}<q<1$, then
$$
\|u-u_p\|_{H^1(\Omega)}\le C_{\mathcal T,d,R,q}M q^p.
$$
This is the fixed-mesh analytic branch; it does not assert an h-dependent estimate or an ordinary Sobolev p-rate on simplices.

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\mathcal T$ be any finite matching shape-regular affine triangulation of a bounded polygonal open set $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^2$, with shape bound $\gamma$ and arbitrary degrees $p_K\ge1$. Set $p_E=\min(p_K,p_{K'})$ on an interior edge, $p_E=p_K$ on a boundary edge, and $m_K=\min_{E\subset\partial K}p_E$. Thus the effective degree retains neighboring shared-trace restrictions, without a bound on degree ratios.

Choose $\chi=1$ and $V=H^1(\Omega)$, or $\chi=0$ and $V=H_0^1(\Omega)$, with Hilbert norm
$$\|v\|_V^2=|v|_{H^1(\Omega)}^2+\chi\|v\|_{L^2(\Omega)}^2.$$
Let $V_{\mathcal T,p}$ be the corresponding conforming hp space, imposing zero boundary traces in the $\chi=0$ branch. Suppose the real bilinear form $a$ and real linear functional $F$ satisfy
$$|a(v,w)|\le M_a\|v\|_V\|w\|_V,\qquad a(v,v)\ge\alpha_a\|v\|_V^2,\qquad \alpha_a>0,$$
with $F$ bounded. Let $u\in V$ be the variational solution and $u_{\mathcal T,p}$ its conforming Galerkin solution. Suppose $u\in C(\overline\Omega)$ and $u|_K\in H^2(K)$; in the zero-boundary branch its continuous representative vanishes on the boundary edges.

For any cellwise comparison polynomials $q_K\in\mathbb P_{m_K}(K)$ put $w_K=u-q_K$ and
$$J_K(q_K)=|w_K|_{H^1(K)}+\sum_{E\subset\partial K}\left(\ell_E^{-1/2}\|w_K\|_{L^2(E)}+\ell_E^{1/2}\|\partial_{\tau_E}w_K\|_{L^2(E)}\right),\qquad R_K(q_K)=h_K^{-1}\|w_K\|_{L^2(K)}+J_K(q_K).$$
Then the actual energy-space error obeys
$$\|u-u_{\mathcal T,p}\|_V\le\frac{M_a}{\alpha_a}C_\gamma\left(\sum_{K\in\mathcal T}\bigl[J_K(q_K)^2+\chi h_K^2R_K(q_K)^2\bigr]\right)^{1/2}.$$
This comparison estimate applies to every degree assignment and the stated piecewise $H^2$ inputs; the comparison polynomials need not match across edges.

For any cellwise integers $s_K\ge2$ with $m_K\ge s_K-1$ and $u|_K\in H^{s_K}(K)$, this also gives the general h-refinement bound
$$\|u-u_{\mathcal T,p}\|_V\le\frac{M_a}{\alpha_a}\left(\sum_K C_{s_K,\gamma}^2(1+\chi h_K^2)h_K^{2(s_K-1)}|u|_{H^{s_K}(K)}^2\right)^{1/2}.$$
In particular every assignment $p_K\ge1$ admits the piecewise $H^2$ estimate with $s_K=2$.

For the additional explicit p-dependent refinement, let integers $r_K\ge5$ satisfy $m_K\ge2r_K-4$, assume $u|_K\in H^{r_K}(K)$, and put $n_K=\lfloor m_K/2\rfloor$ and
$$\eta_{K}=\left(\frac{(n_K-r_K+3)!}{(n_K+r_K-5)!}\right)^{1/2}.$$
There are constants $C_{r_K,\gamma}$ independent of all diameters, degrees and degree ratios such that
$$\|u-u_{\mathcal T,p}\|_V\le\frac{M_a}{\alpha_a}\left(\sum_{K\in\mathcal T}C_{r_K,\gamma}^2(1+\chi h_K^2)h_K^{2(r_K-1)}\eta_K^2|u|_{H^{r_K}(K)}^2\right)^{1/2}.$$
If $m_K\ge4(r_K-2)$, one may replace $\eta_K$ by $(4/m_K)^{r_K-4}$. For a common regularity $r$, this displays local $h_K^{r-1}$ and the proved conservative trace-degree factor $m_K^{-(r-4)}$. It does not claim the optimal $p^{-(r-1)}$ rate or any bound on growth of $C_{r,\gamma}$ as $r\to\infty$. The separate fixed-mesh tensor-analytic and weighted-corner exponential results remain independent branches.

items.title: GLL spectral-element energy error retains the quadrature defect
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega$ have a fixed finite matching affine tensor-box mesh with cell degrees $p_K\ge1$, and let $V_p$ be its trace-matching hp space. On $V=H^1(\Omega)$ use $a(v,w)=\int_\Omega(\nabla v\cdot\nabla w+vw)$ and a bounded load $F$. Define the discrete form on $V_p$ by
$$
a_p(v_p,w_p)=\sum_{K\in\mathcal T}\left(a_{K,p_K}(v_p|_K,w_p|_K)+m_{K,p_K}(v_p|_K,w_p|_K)\right),
$$
using the GLL stiffness and mass forms from [[def-legendre-gauss-lobatto-rule-on-affine-boxes]]. Let $u$ solve the exact variational problem and let $u_p\in V_p$ solve $a_p(u_p,w_p)=F(w_p)$ for every $w_p\in V_p$, with the exact load restricted to $V_p$. Define the form defect $\delta_{a,p}$ by [[def-variational-crime-error-framework]]. Then
$$\|u-u_p\|_{H^1(\Omega)} \le \inf_{v_p\in V_p}\bigl(2\|u-v_p\|_{H^1(\Omega)}+\delta_{a,p}(v_p)\bigr).$$
The stability factor is uniform in all cell degrees. The defect is retained as stated; no aliasing or p-decay estimate is asserted, and GLL assembly is not identified with exact Galerkin assembly.

items.title: An analytic box solution has exponential Galerkin p convergence
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice.

On the single reference square $\Omega=(-1,1)^2$ let $u(x,y)=1/(4-x)$ and use $a(v,w)=\int_\Omega(\nabla v\cdot\nabla w+vw)$ on $H^1(\Omega)$ with exact load $F(w)=a(u,w)$. For every $p\ge1$, the tensor-degree-$p$ conforming Galerkin solution $u_p$ satisfies
$$
\|u-u_p\|_{H^1(\Omega)}\le C\,\frac13\left(\frac34\right)^p
$$
for a fixed constant $C$.
